SELECTED_INDEX: 3
CONFIDENCE: 0.35
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows a strong C=O stretch at 1752 cm⁻¹, typical for a carbonyl in an ester / α-substituted ketone.  A pair of characteristic nitro-group bands is present: a strong νas(NO₂) at 1550 cm⁻¹ and a strong νs(NO₂) at 1298 cm⁻¹.  Only candidate 3 (CCOC(=O)C(CO)[N+](=O)[O-]) contains both a carbonyl and an NO₂ group; all other candidates lack the nitro group and therefore cannot account for the 1550/1300 cm⁻¹ doublet.  Additional medium/strong bands at 1100, 1057, 1011, 913 and 859 cm⁻¹ fit the expected C–O and NO₂ bending/rocking modes of an alkoxy-substituted nitro-ketone, and the C–H stretching/bending region (3022–2888 cm⁻¹, 1454–1434 cm⁻¹) matches the aliphatic groups in candidate 3.  Hence candidate 3 best matches the observed Raman features.
